title: How many people to match my birthday?
hook: 23 people make a shared birthday a coin flip. What about one that matches yours?

knows: in a room of 23 some two people share a birthday about half the time (birthday-paradox)
doesNotKnow: that matching one specific date is a different, slower problem
that the paradox comes from counting pairs

misconception: If 23 people give 50% for some pair to match, 23 people also give about 50% that someone shares my birthday.
objective: The learner can say that 23 people make 253 pairs but only 23 comparisons with you, so matching you needs about 253 people.
keyState: Crowd of 23 (any-match bar 50.7%, your bar 6.1%), 183 (39.5%) and 253 (50.0%).

claims.text: The model uses 365 equally likely birthdays and ignores leap days and uneven birth rates.
With 23 other people, some two of them share a birthday 50.7% of the time, but someone shares yours only 6.1% of the time.
claims.source: 1 - prod_{i<23}(1 - i/365) = 0.5073; 1 - (364/365)^23 = 0.0612 (pAny, pMe in model.ts; recomputed in node).

claims.text: With 183 other people, someone shares your birthday 39.5% of the time.
With 253 other people, someone shares your birthday 50.0% of the time; 252 gives 49.9%, so 253 is the smallest crowd with even odds.
23 other people make 253 pairs among themselves, but you take part in only 23 comparisons; each matches with chance 1 in 365.
claims.source: 23 x 22 / 2 = 253 pairs; you versus 23 others = 23 comparisons; each other person matches you with probability 1/365. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): DISPUTED. The lesson's crowd is 23 OTHER people (pMe(23) = 1-(364/365)^23 = 6.1%). The 253 pairs are among those 23, and you are in none of them; your 23 comparisons are extra pairs. With you included there are 24 people, 276 pairs, 23 involving you; if the 23 includes you, you are in 22 of the 253. 'You are in only 23 of them' is wrong either way. Same sentence is in the reveal ({SMALL} people make {pairs(SMALL)} pairs, but you are in only {SMALL} of them). Suggested fix (builder, claim + reveal): '23 other people make 253 pairs among themselves, but you take part in only 23 comparisons; each matches with chance 1 in 365.' Retracts the pass-8 verification of the earlier wording. | v2 (2026-10-14, builder): rewritten per pass 19 in the claim and the reveal; the crowd is 23 others, so the 253 pairs (23 × 22 / 2) are among them and you are in none; your 23 comparisons are separate. Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 20): Reveal line 84 matches: {SMALL} other people make {pairs(SMALL)} = 253 pairs among themselves, you take part in {SMALL} = 23 comparisons, each 1 in 365. Stage subtitles agree (n comparisons; n(n-1)/2 pairs). Own node: pairs(23) = 253, pMe(23) = 6.1%, pAny(23) = 50.7%.

claims.text: It takes about 253 comparisons with you to reach even odds.
Each other person misses your birthday with chance 364/365; with 253 people the chance that none match is (364/365)^253, about 50%.
claims.source: Independent misses multiply: (364/365)^253 = 0.4995. The 253 equals 23 x 22 / 2 by coincidence.

recall.question: A class has 30 students. Which is more likely: some two students share a birthday, or someone shares YOUR birthday?
recall.why: 30 people make 435 pairs, but only 30 comparisons involve you. Some pair matching is about 71%; someone matching you is about 8%.
